_note: Life events. Each arrives as a call, text or moment in the dressing room, with choices that cost something. Effects: honour, manager, teammates, fans, family, money, energy, slot (uses a time slot this week), flag (remembered), unflag. 'next' queues a follow-up {id, in: weeks, chance}. 'news' puts a story in Monday's paper: page front|back, headline with {NAME}. Conditions: minWeek, notPreseason, needFlag, notFlag, meter minimums (min) / maximums (max), contract types (types), weight. Design rule: the bad choice is always tempting.

events.text: Mate. Overslept. Again. If the gaffer asks, tell him I was with you at the physio. You're a legend. Owe you one. Gaz

choices.label: Cover for him
choices.result: Gaz owes you one. Gaz has owed everyone one since 2019.

choices.label: Tell him to sort himself out
choices.result: Gaz calls you a grass in the group chat. Then sends a sad face.

events.text: Funny thing, son. The physio was in Tenerife last Tuesday. So where were you and Gaz? Think carefully. I can smell a lie like a three-day-old mackerel.

choices.label: Come clean
choices.result: The gaffer nods slowly. Gaz runs laps until his legs are spaghetti.

choices.label: Double down on the lie
choices.result: The gaffer's eyes narrow. You've been dropped into his bad books, and the bad books are wet.

events.text: Quick one, pet. Are you starting Saturday? Only Maureen at bingo reckons you're on the bench and there's good money riding on it. Just a little nod. Nobody would know.

choices.label: Give her a little nod
choices.result: Gran makes a noise like a kettle. 'You're a good boy.'

choices.label: Gran, I can't tell you that
choices.result: 'Your grandad would've told me,' she says. Your grandad was banned from three bookmakers.

events.text: They've BANNED me from the bookies! Said my bets were 'statistically improbable'. I said I'm just lucky. They've sent a letter to the FA. Is that bad?

choices.label: Ring the FA and explain
choices.result: A tired man at the FA writes 'GRAN' on a Post-it and sighs.

news.headline: GRANNY GAMBLE: {NAME}'S NAN IN BETTING BAN

choices.label: Lie low and hope it goes away
choices.result: It doesn't go away. It never goes away.

events.text: Hi! We'd love you to visit the children's ward on Thursday. Bring a smile and some signed photos. (Gaz says the lads are going to Wetherspoons that night. Ignore Gaz.)

choices.label: Visit the hospital (uses a time slot)
choices.result: A seven-year-old beats you at FIFA and tells you you're rubbish. Best afternoon of your life.

news.headline: HEARTS OF GOLD: {NAME} CHEERS SICK KIDS

choices.label: Go out with the lads
choices.result: Somebody orders a round of Jägerbombs at 6pm. It's a long night.

events.text: Sid Scoop, Weekly Splash. I've got a photo of you asleep in a kebab shop wearing a traffic cone. Any comment before we go to print?

choices.label: 'It was a fancy dress thing'
choices.result: It was not a fancy dress thing.

choices.label: Apologise to the club
choices.result: The gaffer accepts. He's seen worse. He did worse.

news.headline: SORRY SEEMS TO BE THE HARDEST WORD FOR CONE-HEAD {NAME}

events.text: You're live on Radio Bantam's Football Phone-In! Caller from Dudley says the gaffer's tactics are 'like watching paint dry, but the paint's also asleep'. Do you agree?

choices.label: Back the gaffer
choices.result: The gaffer texts you a single fish emoji. High praise.

choices.label: 'He's got a point, to be fair'
choices.result: The phone-in lines light up. So does the gaffer's face.

choices.label: Talk about fishing for ten minutes
choices.result: The presenter cuts to the travel news. The gaffer loved it.

events.text: It's my birthday dinner Wednesday love. Your auntie Carol's coming. She's bringing the trifle. Please come. The coach mentioned extra shooting practice though didn't he?

choices.label: Go to Mum's dinner (uses a time slot)
choices.result: Auntie Carol's trifle is 40% sherry. Mum cries twice. Lovely evening.

choices.label: Stay for extra shooting
choices.result: Mum says it's fine. It is not fine. Auntie Carol posts about it on Facebook.

events.text: Initiation night. Everyone's chanting your name. You have to stand on a chair and sing. The senior pros are watching. Gaz is filming.

choices.label: Belt out Mr Brightside
choices.result: You miss every high note. The dressing room goes wild. Gaz's video gets 40 views, all Gaz.

choices.label: Refuse, you're not a performing seal
choices.result: Silence. Someone fills your boots with yoghurt the next morning.

events.text: Hi, Nikey Sports here (not that one). We'll give you £600 to wear our boots. They're nearly leather. The swoosh goes the other way. Interested?

choices.label: Take the £600
choices.result: The boots squeak. Every step sounds like a duck being sat on.

news.headline: JUST DON'T DO IT: {NAME}'S KNOCK-OFF BOOT DEAL

choices.label: No thanks
choices.result: 'Your loss,' they text. Then: 'Would you do it for £400?'

events.text: You're in the big Tesco in your pyjama bottoms buying Coco Pops when a fan spots you. 'Can I get a selfie? And can you do a video for my brother? He hates you.'

choices.label: Smile, selfie, video, the lot
choices.result: The brother still hates you, but he hates you a bit less.

choices.label: Pretend you're someone else
choices.result: 'You're definitely him,' she says. 'You've got his face.'

news.headline: PYJAMA DRAMA: {NAME} SNUBS FAN IN CEREAL AISLE

events.text: Son. I'm going down the reservoir Sunday. Dawn start. Bring a flask. Don't tell the others, they'll want to come and they fish like idiots.

choices.label: Go fishing with the gaffer (uses a time slot)
choices.result: Six hours. One fish. He names it after you. It's the happiest you've ever seen him.

choices.label: Make an excuse
choices.result: 'Suit yourself,' he says, in the voice of a man who will remember this.

events.text: Big Terry, club captain, 34, has taken your peg, your towel and your protein shake. 'Rookies get the corner by the bin,' he says. The lads are watching.

choices.label: Stand up to him
choices.result: Big Terry stares at you for a long time. Then he laughs and gives you the towel back. The shake's gone though.

choices.label: Corner by the bin it is
choices.result: It's not too bad by the bin. You get to know the bin quite well.

events.text: Oi superstar. The Red Lion are in the cup final Sunday and we're short. Come on, one game, for old times. Ref's blind. Pitch is a swamp. You'll love it.

choices.label: Play for the Red Lion (uses a time slot)
choices.result: You score a hat-trick in wellies. Deano cries. You're banned from the Red Lion's car park for life (long story).

choices.label: Can't risk the injury, sorry
choices.result: Deano sends a voice note. It's just him saying 'Big time Charlie' for forty seconds.

events.text: Someone's sent me a video of you in a Red Lion shirt, on a swamp, doing a knee slide into a dog. Explain.

choices.label: 'It was for charity'
choices.result: 'Which charity?' 'The Red Lion.' Long silence.

news.headline: PUB-LIC ENEMY: {NAME} RISKS IT ALL IN SUNDAY LEAGUE

choices.label: Hold your hands up
choices.result: He fines you a week's tea money. Fair.

events.text: Bro can I borrow £500. Car's failed its MOT and I need it for, er, a car thing. Pay you back next week 100%. Kev

choices.label: Lend him £500
choices.result: Kev hugs you so hard your back clicks.

choices.label: Sorry Kev, skint
choices.result: Kev says no worries. Kev is very worried.

events.text: Told you bro! £500 back plus a Twix for interest. Legend.

choices.label: Accept the Twix
choices.result: Best interest rate you'll ever get.

events.text: The prank war's escalated. Somebody's put cling film over the gaffer's toilet. Everyone thinks it was you. It wasn't. Was it?

choices.label: Go bigger: fill Gaz's car with balloons
choices.result: Four hundred balloons. Gaz opens the door and becomes a viral sensation.

choices.label: Stay well out of it
choices.result: You eat your lunch alone, but with dignity.

events.text: Dear former pupil. We'd love you to present the prizes at Prize Day. Mr Hargreaves (PE) says he 'always knew'. He did not always know.

choices.label: Present the prizes (uses a time slot)
choices.result: Mr Hargreaves calls you 'my lad'. Your old maths teacher asks for a selfie. Revenge tastes like Ribena.

news.headline: HEAD OF THE CLASS: {NAME} BACK AT SCHOOL

choices.label: Too busy, sorry
choices.result: They get the local weatherman instead. He's thrilled.

events.text: Sid Scoop. I'll write you a lovely puff piece. 'Wonderkid', the works. All I need is the team for Saturday. Who's playing? Tiny thing. Nobody gets hurt.

choices.label: Leak the team
choices.result: Sid sends you £200 in an envelope that smells of pickled onions.

choices.label: Tell Sid where to go
choices.result: 'You'll regret that,' says Sid. You suspect he's right.

events.text: Somebody leaked my team to Sid Scoop. I've narrowed it down to you, Gaz and the bloke who does the pies. The pie bloke can't read. And Gaz can't spell 'team'.

choices.label: Confess
choices.result: He doesn't shout. That's worse. He just sighs, like a slow puncture.

choices.label: Blame the pie bloke
choices.result: The pie bloke is sacked. The pies are worse now. Everyone knows.

events.text: I won again on you, pet! I've bought you a present. It's a gold chain. It's very big. It says your name. In diamonds. Well, nearly diamonds.

choices.label: Wear it with pride
choices.result: It weighs more than your boots. The lads call you Mr T.

news.headline: BLING IT ON: {NAME}'S GRAN GOES FOR GOLD

choices.label: Thank her, hide it in a drawer
choices.result: Gran checks every photo of you for the chain. Every. Photo.

events.text: Love, the club nutritionist rang. She says you've been living on Pot Noodles. I've booked you a cooking class with Auntie Carol. Thursday. It's non-negotiable. x

choices.label: Go to the cooking class (uses a time slot)
choices.result: You learn three meals. Two involve sherry.

choices.label: Order a Deliveroo instead
choices.result: Your Deliveroo rider recognises you and asks why you're always ordering chicken nuggets at 11pm.

events.text: Congratulations! You've been voted Supporters' Player of the Month! The award ceremony is at the Working Men's Club. There'll be a buffet. A big one.

choices.label: Go and give a speech
choices.result: You thank your mum, your gran and the buffet. Standing ovation.

choices.label: Send a video message
choices.result: The video plays sideways. Everyone watches it sideways.

events.text: A bloke in the car park shouts 'Get a proper striker!' at you. His mate shouts 'Or a proper haircut!' Then they ask for an autograph for their kid.

choices.label: Sign it, and smile
choices.result: 'You're alright, you,' says the first bloke. Progress.

choices.label: Tell them what you think of them
choices.result: Someone films it. It's not your best angle.

news.headline: CAR PARK CLASH: {NAME} BLOWS HIS TOP

events.text: Tony here. Super-agent. Lunch. My treat. Steakhouse. I've got contacts in Dubai, Madrid and a bloke in Rhyl. Sign nothing, just eat.

choices.label: Go to lunch
choices.result: Tony orders for you, takes a photo of you, and leaves you with the bill. £180.

choices.label: Ignore him
choices.result: Tony sends you 14 voice notes. One is just him chewing.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Funny photo landed on my desk: you, a steakhouse, and Tony 'Ten Percent' Malone. Are you leaving the club?

choices.label: 'No comment'
choices.result: 'No comment' means yes in newspaper.

choices.label: 'I love this club'
choices.result: Sid prints it anyway, with a photo of you holding a steak knife.

events.text: Dennis grabs your arm in the corridor. 'Tuesday. A seagull. Don't eat the sausage roll.' He walks off. On Tuesday a seagull steals your sausage roll. Dennis winks at you from across the car park.

choices.label: Ask Dennis what else he knows
choices.result: 'You'll be famous,' he says. 'Or infamous. Depends on the slippers.' What slippers?

choices.label: Back away slowly
choices.result: You start checking for seagulls everywhere. There are always seagulls.

events.text: Mate. Hear me out. Vape shop. For DOGS. Flavours: bacon, postman, next door's cat. I just need £500 to get started. You'll get 20%. Of the profits. Of the dogs.

choices.label: Invest £500
choices.result: Deano cries. He promises you'll be 'on the ground floor'. The ground floor is his mum's garage.

choices.label: Not a chance
choices.result: Deano says you've 'changed'. You have. You've learned what a dog vape is.

events.text: Dog vapes didn't work (RSPCA got involved). BUT. Novelty slippers. Shaped like YOUR face. Fans will go mad. I've found a supplier. Minimum order 40,000. I need £5,000. This is the one.

choices.label: Back him with £5,000
choices.result: Somewhere in China, a factory starts making 40,000 of your face.

choices.label: Absolutely not
choices.result: Deano finds another investor. It's his nan. Dennis the kit man looks relieved.

events.text: Slight problem. The slippers arrived. They've got your face on, but it's not really your face. It's more like a sad potato. Nobody's buying. They're in your garage. All of them. Also the press know.

choices.label: Laugh it off and sign a few for charity
choices.result: A children's hospital gets 500 signed potato slippers. The kids love them. Deano sells the rest at a car boot for 20p each.

choices.label: Blame Deano in public
choices.result: Deano unfollows you. Then refollows you to unfollow you again, so you notice.

news.headline: SLIPPER-Y SLOPE: {NAME} DUMPS BEST MATE OVER 40,000 FACE SLIPPERS

events.text: PARTY AT MINE SATURDAY 🎉🎉 foam machine CONFIRMED. bring the lads. bring snacks. bring a towel (foam).

choices.label: Go (but leave early, match day)
choices.result: You leave at 10pm. Shaz calls you 'grandad' in the group chat. Worth it.

choices.label: Go all in
choices.result: You wake up covered in foam on a sun lounger. It's Sunday. It might be Monday.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Lovely photos from a foam party. You, a sun lounger, a traffic cone (again), and what looks like a goat. Comment?

choices.label: 'The goat was invited'
choices.result: The goat becomes a minor celebrity.

choices.label: Ask Shaz to make a statement
choices.result: Shaz's statement is a 40-second voice note of her laughing.

events.text: Got a van full of tellies. Don't ask. 75-inch. Hundred quid each. You want one? Your mum wants one. I've already asked your mum.

choices.label: Take a telly (£100)
choices.result: It's a great telly. It has someone else's Netflix logged in.

choices.label: Lee, I can't
choices.result: 'Your loss,' says Lee. 'Ninety quid?'

events.text: Card night at mine Friday. Proper game. Bring cash. My cousin Tel's playing. Don't stare at Tel's eyebrow.

choices.label: I'm in (opens Big Lee's card nights in the Casino)
choices.result: Tel's eyebrow is mesmerising. Big Lee's card nights are now in your Casino menu.

choices.label: Not for me
choices.result: Lee says 'suit yourself' and deals Tel in.

events.text: bro. BRO. need u on my new track. just say 'big ting' 4 times in a deep voice. gonna be massive. trust.

choices.label: Record it
choices.result: The track gets 40,000 plays. 39,000 are people laughing at you. You're a meme. A popular meme.

choices.label: Leave me out of it
choices.result: Ty goes quiet. Ty is never quiet.

events.text: dropped a diss track about u. its called 'Bench Warmer'. no hard feelings. its fire tho.

choices.label: Respond with a diss track of your own
choices.result: Your track rhymes 'bench' with 'bench'. The internet decides you've won anyway.

choices.label: Rise above it
choices.result: Ty's track gets 600 plays. He blames the algorithm.

events.text: I looked at your bank statement (you left it open). You spent £84 on Greggs last week. EIGHTY FOUR. Let me set you up with a savings plan. I'll do it for free. Well, for a sausage roll.

choices.label: Let Priya sort it
choices.result: Priya puts £200 in your rainy day fund and bans you from Greggs on weekdays.

choices.label: I'm fine, honestly
choices.result: You buy a sausage roll to prove a point. It is not a point.

events.text: Grown-up talk: rent is money you never see again. If you buy somewhere sensible, it's an investment. Not a moat. Please don't buy a moat.

choices.label: Listen. Properly.
choices.result: Priya draws a graph. You understand 60% of it. That's 60% more than your agent.

choices.label: 'What about a moat though?'
choices.result: Priya puts her head on the table for a long time.

events.text: Watched your last game. Your left hamstring's tight, you're landing heavy on it. Come round, I'll sort you a routine. Free. I need the practice and you need the hamstring.

choices.label: Go round (uses a time slot)
choices.result: Mo's routine is mostly lying on the floor groaning. You feel brand new.

choices.label: It's fine, I'll stretch
choices.result: You don't stretch.

events.text: The youth club roof's leaking again. We're doing a sponsored penalty shoot-out. Would you go in goal? The kids want to score past a 'real footballer'. Even a striker.

choices.label: Go in goal (uses a time slot)
choices.result: You let in 112 penalties. They raise £2,300. The roof gets fixed. A seven-year-old does a Cristiano celebration in your face.

news.headline: SAVE OF THE DAY: {NAME} LETS IN 112 FOR CHARITY

choices.label: Send a signed shirt
choices.result: The shirt raises £40. It's a nice shirt.

events.text: Son. A word from an old pro. The game'll chew you up if you let it. Look after your mum, save your money, and never trust a man in a long coat who says 'trust me'. That's all. Oh, and wear long studs.

choices.label: Thank him, properly
choices.result: Stan goes quiet, then says 'your grandad would've been proud'. You both pretend you've got something in your eye.

choices.label: 'Cheers Stan' (you're busy)
choices.result: Stan says 'right you are' and tells the same thing to the man in the newsagent.

events.text: We need to talk. You're never here. When you are here, you're watching yourself on Match of the Day. I think we're done.

choices.label: Beg for one more chance (uses a time slot)
choices.result: A long walk, a longer talk, and a chippy tea. You're still together. Just.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.result: It's over. Mum brings round a lasagne. Gran says 'plenty more fish', then 'your grandad would've said that'.

events.text: They're brushing their teeth at yours. Again. 'I've basically moved in,' they say. 'Shall we make it official?'

choices.label: Move in together
choices.result: Their stuff arrives. So does a ferret. Nobody mentioned a ferret.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: 'Fine,' they say. It is not fine. They take their toothbrush home pointedly.

events.text: You've got the ring. It's been in your sock drawer for three weeks. Gran knows. Dennis knows. Somehow Sid Scoop knows. It's now or never.

choices.label: Get down on one knee
choices.result: They say yes before you've finished the question. You were going to say a whole poem.

news.headline: DOWN ON ONE KNEE: {NAME} POPS THE QUESTION

choices.label: Bottle it
choices.result: The ring goes back in the sock. The sock knows.

events.text: The wedding. Big do at a stately home with a swan ice sculpture and the whole squad? Or the registry office and a pub lunch?

choices.label: Big do (£40,000)
choices.result: The swan melts by 3pm. Gaz catches the bouquet. Gran wins £200 on the length of the best man's speech.

choices.label: Registry office and the Red Lion
choices.result: Deano does the speech. It's mostly about dog vapes. Perfect.

events.text: 3am. A stunning stranger in the VIP bit is laughing at all your jokes, even the one about the dog vapes. 'Come back to mine?' Your partner thinks you're at Gaz's.

choices.label: Go back to theirs
choices.result: It's exciting. Then it's 9am and you feel sick, and not from the Jägerbombs.

choices.label: Get a taxi home
choices.result: You're home by 3.30. Your partner's asleep with the ferret. You've never been happier.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Got photos of you leaving a flat at 9am in last night's clothes. Not your flat. Not your partner's flat. Story runs Monday. Comment?

choices.label: Tell your partner before the paper does
choices.result: There's a lot of shouting. Some crying. The ferret takes their side.

news.headline: LOVE RAT {NAME} IN 9AM WALK OF SHAME

choices.label: Deny everything
choices.result: The photos are very clear. You are very not clear.

news.headline: LIAR, LIAR: CHEAT {NAME}'S DENIAL IN TATTERS

events.text: Your new teammates keep laughing at something you said in training. The interpreter explains: you've been calling the gaffer 'my little cabbage' all week.

choices.label: Book language lessons (uses a time slot)
choices.result: Three weeks later you can order a coffee, apologise to the gaffer, and swear fluently. In that order.

choices.label: Keep smiling and nodding
choices.result: You agree to a lot of things. One of them, it turns out, was carrying the kit bags until Christmas.

events.text: Are you eating, love? I've posted you a box: PG Tips, Branston, a Greggs steak bake (it might not survive) and a photo of the dog. Your Gran says the foreign food will make you soft.

choices.label: Video call for an hour
choices.result: The dog licks the screen. You cry a bit. Nobody needs to know.

choices.label: Too busy, text her later
choices.result: The steak bake arrives three weeks later. It has become a different substance.

events.text: A local journalist asks, through a translator, whether you prefer it here or back home. The whole city will read the answer.

choices.label: 'I love it here, this is my home now'
choices.result: The city loves you. Your mum reads it on Google Translate and goes quiet for a day.

choices.label: 'Nothing beats a rainy Tuesday in England'
choices.result: The headline translates roughly as 'ENGLISHMAN SAYS OUR WEATHER IS BAD'. Which, to be fair, it isn't.

events.text: Mate. Tiny favour. Get yourself booked in the first ten minutes Saturday. That's it. A little yellow card. My cousin's got a bet on. £5,000 in your hand. Nobody gets hurt. It's a yellow card.

choices.label: Take the £5,000
choices.result: Lee gives you an envelope in a Greggs bag. You get booked for a 'clumsy challenge' in the seventh minute. Your heart is going like the clappers.

choices.label: Absolutely not
choices.result: Lee laughs it off. 'Only joking.' He wasn't joking.

events.text: That went beautiful. Now my cousin's mate wants something bigger. Miss a penalty. Just one. £20,000. You're in it now, son. Be a shame if anyone found out about the yellow card.

choices.label: Do it (£20,000)
choices.result: You blaze it over the bar. The crowd groans. You feel sick for a week.

choices.label: Go to the FA yourself
choices.result: The FA thank you for your honesty. You get a six-week ban for the yellow card. Lee stops speaking to you. The papers call you 'the whistleblower'.

events.text: The FA's integrity unit would like a word about some unusual betting patterns. On you. A yellow card and a penalty. They have phone records. And a Greggs bag.

choices.label: Confess everything
choices.result: A ten-month ban. Your name is mud. But it's over, and you told the truth.

news.headline: SHAME OF {NAME}: STRIKER BANNED FOR MATCH FIXING

choices.label: Deny it
choices.result: Your lawyer says 'it'll be fine'. It is not fine.

events.text: Guilty. Conspiracy to defraud. The judge looks at you over her glasses: 'You had everything, and you threw it away for a Greggs bag.' Eighteen months, out in nine.

choices.label: Go down quietly
choices.result: Prison is a chapter, not the end. You'll be out in nine months. Then the hard part starts.

events.text: VIP offer for our favourite customer! £20,000 credit line, no checks, no questions. Win it all back this weekend!

choices.label: Take the credit
choices.result: It feels like free money. It isn't free and it isn't money.

choices.label: Delete the app
choices.result: You delete it. Then you delete the other three. Priya is very proud.

events.text: The odds on your team losing Saturday are 4/1. You're owed £24,000. You know the team news. One bet would clear it all.

choices.label: Place the bet
choices.result: You win. Then the FA's systems flag it within the hour.

news.headline: {NAME} BET AGAINST OWN TEAM: FA BAN

choices.label: Get help instead
choices.result: You ring a gambling helpline at 2am. A woman called Pat talks to you for an hour. You owe Pat everything.

events.from: A man in a long coat
events.text: I represent a much bigger club. I can't say which. It rhymes with 'Smarsenal'. We'd love a quiet coffee. Nobody needs to know.

choices.label: Take the meeting quietly
choices.result: The coffee is lovely. The offer is lovelier. You leave by the back door, like a spy.

choices.label: Report it to your club
choices.result: The chairman is touched. He gives you a framed photo of himself. You didn't want it.

choices.label: Leak it to force a move
choices.result: It's on every back page by Thursday. The fans burn a replica shirt. It doesn't burn well (polyester).

news.headline: GET ME OUT: {NAME} WANTS BIG MOVE

events.text: Sid Scoop. Lovely photo of you leaving a coffee shop by the back door. With a man in a long coat. Fancy explaining?

choices.label: 'I was buying a coffee'
choices.result: Nobody believes you. Not even the barista.

news.headline: TAPPED UP! {NAME} IN SECRET COFFEE SUMMIT

choices.label: Come clean to the gaffer
choices.result: He sighs. 'Everyone's got a price, son. Just don't make me find out from Sid Scoop next time.'

events.text: Gaz's other half has had a few. She's been flirting with you all night, and now she's suggesting you 'get some air' together. Gaz is in the kitchen doing his dance.

choices.label: Get some air together
choices.result: It's a bad idea and you both know it. You do it anyway.

choices.label: Find Gaz and go and dance badly
choices.result: You and Gaz dance until 3am. It's horrific. It's the right choice.

events.text: Gaz knows. Everyone knows. Nobody's passing to you in training. Gaz threw a boot at you. Then the other boot.

choices.label: Apologise to Gaz in front of everyone
choices.result: He doesn't accept it. But the lads respect that you stood there and took it.

news.headline: LOVE RAT {NAME}: AFFAIR WITH TEAMMATE'S PARTNER

choices.label: Ask for a transfer
choices.result: The dressing room has collapsed. The gaffer has gone fishing and isn't answering.

events.text: The forehead's winning. Gaz has started calling you 'The Moon'. A clinic in Istanbul does a package: flights, hotel, 4,000 grafts and a bandana. £6,000.

choices.label: Book the flights
choices.result: Six weeks in a bandana. Then: hair! Actual hair! Gaz has to find a new nickname.

choices.label: Shave it all off and own it
choices.result: You look like a Bond villain. A handsome one. Your partner approves.

events.text: Sid Scoop. Funny photo: you, an airport, a bandana. Want to tell the nation about your 'holiday'?

choices.label: 'Yes, I had a hair transplant. Look at it!'
choices.result: The honesty goes down a storm. The clinic sends you a fruit basket.

news.headline: HAIR TODAY: {NAME} COMES CLEAN OVER TURKEY TRANSPLANT

choices.result: The internet zooms in on your scalp. The internet is merciless.

events.text: They hand you a little stick with two lines on it. 'So,' they say. 'That happened.'

choices.label: Cry happy tears
choices.result: You both cry. Then you ring your mum. Then she cries. Then Gran puts a bet on the name.

choices.label: Panic, then cry happy tears
choices.result: You go white, sit down, stand up, sit down, then hug them for ten minutes.

events.text: "Dad, you missed my birthday. Mum said you were at training. It's fine. Grandma made the cake."
